subject: Data residency and private deployment controls for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@nimbushealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Data residency & private deployment controls – Nimbus Health

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As we evaluate Redwood for PHI-adjacent workloads, our security/compliance team has a few focused questions around region guarantees and private networking that we need to resolve before procurement. I've attached our SIG-style spreadsheet with specific asks, but the immediate ones are: 

- Can you confirm that for a Redwood Private deployment we can restrict processing and storage to eu-west-1 (Ireland) and prevent any cross-region backups or metadata egress?
- Do you offer VPC peering or PrivateLink-style connectivity so we can avoid public internet egress?
- How is KMS/HSM integration handled for customer keys (BYOK) in the private deployment?
- What audit logs are available (token-level, request path, K/V cache ops) and how long are they retained in Private vs Dedicated?

We need short, attributable statements for our procurement and InfoSec team and any supporting artifacts (SOC 2 summary, architecture diagram). Can you also indicate typical lead times for a private VPC onboarding?

Appreciate a response by Friday if possible — our procurement window is tight.

Best,
Emma
Security Lead, Nimbus Health
[Attachment: nimbus-sig-questions.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@nimbushealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency & private deployment controls – Nimbus Health

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the spreadsheet. Looping in Neha (security) and Priyom (solutions) to provide the detailed confirmations and artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, Private deployments can be constrained to a single cloud region (we support region pinning to eu-west-1).
- We offer private connectivity options (VPC peering and an AWS PrivateLink-equivalent for supported clouds).
- BYOK with customer-managed KMS is supported; we integrate with KMIP/KMS APIs and can provide HSM-backed keys in many engagements.

Neha/Priyom — can you attach the SOC 2 one-page and the architecture sketch that addresses cross-region backups, egress controls, and audit log retention? Also please confirm lead time for onboarding (targeting < 6 weeks for standard private deployments, contingent on accounts paperwork).

Emma — we'll produce concise, attributable statements that you can paste into your SIG/CAIQ responses.

- Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@nimbushealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency & private deployment controls – Nimbus Health

Emma — thanks for the spreadsheet. I reviewed the asks and summarized our positions below with explicit wording you can paste into SIG/CAIQ cells. I've attached a short SOC 2 summary and the private deployment architecture diagram.

1) Region residency statement
"Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) processes and stores customer data exclusively in the cloud region selected by the customer. For Nimbus Health, Redwood will configure and operate the deployment within eu-west-1 (Ireland) with controls in place to prevent automated cross-region replication. Any manual or emergency cross-region movement requires documented change control and customer authorization."

2) Backups and cross-region copies
"Automated backups for Private deployments are configurable by the customer. By default we provision region-local snapshot-based backups that remain in the same region. Cross-region replication is disabled by default; enabling replication requires an explicit configuration change and dual-authorization approval."

3) Private connectivity and egress controls
"Redwood supports VPC peering and provider-managed PrivateLink endpoints. All control plane traffic that crosses networks is tunneled over mutually authenticated TLS or private link connectors; no unencrypted public internet egress is required. Customers can enforce egress block lists at the VPC level."

4) KMS/BYOK
"Customers may bring their own keys via cloud provider KMS or an HSM. Redwood supports key wrapping and never stores plaintext customer keys. We can operate in a zero-key-access mode where cryptographic operations are performed in the customer key domain."

5) Audit logs and retention
"Private deployments expose token-level request logs, model selection traces, authentication events, and system telemetry. Default retention is 90 days for high-fidelity logs; extended retention options are available as an add-on. All logs can be exported to a customer-controlled S3 bucket or SIEM via secure transfer."

6) Evidence and artifacts
"Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (one-page SOC 2 scope & audit status), private-deploy-arch-diagram.png (architecture, VPC flows), and a sample SIG mapping spreadsheet. For SOC 2 report delivery (full report) we require an NDA and MSA addendum flagging report delivery; summary artifacts are attached for immediate use."

7) Onboarding lead time
"Typical onboarding for a standard Private deployment is 4–6 weeks from signed MSA and receipt of network details/CIDR allocations. Faster timelines (2–3 weeks) are possible with pre-approved templates and dedicated onboarding slots."

Please let me know if you want any of the statements tweaked to match Nimbus legal language.

- Neha
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF), private-deploy-arch-diagram.png (PNG)]
